nodes.name: app.py
nodes.summary: Flask web dashboard for the live production system, exposing routes that render capital, costs, FX, P&L, process status, reconciliation, rolls, risk and trades views backed by the reporting API.
nodes.languageNotes: Flask app using before/after request hooks (get_data/cleanup_data) and asyncio event-loop setup per request for broker calls.

nodes.name: processes
nodes.summary: Builds the process-control overview by combining config, control and process status tables plus trading-server login data into a JSON response.

nodes.name: reconcile
nodes.summary: Assembles a reconciliation view comparing optimal, IB broker and internal positions for the trades dashboard.

nodes.name: rolls_post
nodes.summary: Handles POST roll actions, computing current/updated multiple and adjusted prices and applying roll-state changes for the selected instrument.

nodes.name: trades
nodes.summary: Compiles order overview, delays and slippage tables (raw, vol, cash) into a JSON payload for the trades view.

nodes.name: pandl
nodes.summary: Returns P&L tables across instruments, strategies and sectors for the dashboard P&L view.

nodes.name: dict_of_df_to_dict
nodes.summary: Utility converting a dict of DataFrames into a JSON-serialisable nested dict using a chosen pandas orient.

nodes.name: broker_execution_stack.py
nodes.summary: Abstract broker execution stack interface defining the contract for placing, matching, cancelling and modifying broker orders, to be implemented per-broker (e.g. IB).

nodes.name: brokerExecutionStackData
nodes.summary: Abstract base for broker order-stack access, declaring NotImplemented methods for listing, matching, cancelling and modifying broker orders.

nodes.name: list_running_pids.py
nodes.summary: Lists running process IDs either locally (via psutil) or remotely (via SSH subprocess) to support the production process monitor.

nodes.name: remote_list_of_running_pids
nodes.summary: Runs an SSH command against the trading server to fetch the list of running Python PIDs over the network.

nodes.name: describe_trading_server_login_data
nodes.summary: Produces a human-readable description of the configured trading-server SSH login details.

nodes.name: monitor.py
nodes.summary: Continuously monitors all production processes, updating per-process status and rendering an HTML status page for the live trading system.

nodes.name: processMonitor
nodes.summary: Tracks and updates the running status of every control process, logging status changes and producing HTML tables/messages.

nodes.name: generate_html
nodes.summary: Writes the monitor status HTML page combining process tables and log messages to disk.

nodes.name: report_process_status.py
nodes.summary: Throttled status-logging helpers that record process wait conditions and avoid log spam by tracking last-log timing per status key.

nodes.name: reportStatus
nodes.summary: Base throttled logger that records status messages only when enough time has elapsed, tracking per-key last-log timestamps.

nodes.name: reportProcessStatus
nodes.summary: Specialises reportStatus to log and clear process wait conditions keyed by reason and condition.

nodes.name: run_process.py
nodes.summary: Core production process runner: manages start/wait gating, the main loop over timer methods, pause/stop handling and clean finish for a scheduled trading process.
nodes.languageNotes: Heavy use of free functions operating on a processToRun object to keep the control-flow logic flat and testable.

nodes.name: processToRun
nodes.summary: Encapsulates a runnable production process, wiring its timer functions, control data and diagnostics and driving the run/finish lifecycle.

nodes.name: _check_if_process_status_is_okay_to_run
nodes.summary: Checks control-status flags (start allowed, time, previous run) and reports wait conditions to decide whether a process may start.

nodes.name: _check_if_okay_to_wait_before_starting_process
nodes.summary: Determines whether the process should wait rather than start, reporting and clearing wait conditions accordingly.

nodes.name: _check_for_stop
nodes.summary: Evaluates stop conditions (control-process stop, all methods finished, finish time) to decide when to end the run loop.

nodes.name: wait_for_next_method_run_time
nodes.summary: Sleeps until the next scheduled timer method is due, flushing stdout for log visibility.

nodes.name: strategy_tools.py
nodes.summary: Resolves and instantiates per-strategy class instances and methods from production config so processes can dispatch to strategy-specific logic.

nodes.name: strategyRunner
nodes.summary: Wraps a strategy's configured class/method so a production process can invoke the right strategy code with resolved arguments.

nodes.name: get_class_object_and_other_arguments
nodes.summary: Reads production config to resolve the strategy class object and its extra constructor arguments for a process.

nodes.name: timer_functions.py
nodes.summary: Defines the timer abstraction that decides when each process method should run, tracking run frequency, run-on-start/exit and completion state.

nodes.name: timerClassWithFunction
nodes.summary: Wraps a single process method with its scheduling parameters, deciding when to run it and tracking its last/next run and finished state.

nodes.name: listOfTimerFunctions
nodes.summary: Collection of timerClassWithFunction objects with helpers for next-run timing and all-finished checks across a process.

nodes.name: get_list_of_timer_functions
nodes.summary: Builds the list of timer functions for a named process from its configured methods and parameters.

nodes.name: timer_parameters.py
nodes.summary: Small dataclass holding the scheduling parameters (frequency, run-on-start/exit flags) for a single process timer.

nodes.name: constants.py
nodes.summary: Defines named_object sentinel values and a status type used as lightweight typed constants throughout the codebase.

nodes.name: date_input.py
nodes.summary: Interactive command-line helpers for prompting the user for report dates and datetime values with sensible defaults.

nodes.name: get_report_dates
nodes.summary: Interactively prompts the user to choose a reporting date range (rolling, calendar or custom) for production reports.

nodes.name: get_datetime_input
nodes.summary: Prompts and validates a single datetime (or date) value from the user with an optional default.

nodes.name: display.py
nodes.summary: Text-display utilities for the CLI: centring, landing strips, width measurement and pandas print options for nicely formatted console output.

nodes.name: centralise_text
nodes.summary: Centres a string within a given width using a fill character for tidy console output.

nodes.name: calculate_multiplication_factor_for_nice_repr_of_value
nodes.summary: Computes a scaling factor so small float values are displayed with a readable number of significant digits.

nodes.name: menus.py
nodes.summary: Interactive console menu system letting the user pick options from lists or dict-based menus, used by production interactive scripts.

nodes.name: interactiveMenu
nodes.summary: Stateful nested menu driver that presents grouped options and returns the user's chosen action across menu levels.

nodes.name: print_menu_and_get_desired_option_index
nodes.summary: Prints a dict-based menu and returns the index of the option the user selects, honouring a default.

nodes.name: text.py
nodes.summary: String/text utilities including underscore-aware key sorting, underscore stripping, argument-length normalisation and camelCase splitting.

nodes.name: force_args_to_same_length
nodes.summary: Normalises a set of argument lists to the same length by padding so they can be zipped together.

nodes.name: sort_keywords_by_underscore_length
nodes.summary: Sorts keyword strings by their number of leading underscores to order config keys consistently.

nodes.name: csv_spot_fx.py
nodes.summary: CSV-backed implementation of spot FX price storage, reading and writing currency price series to disk for backtests and data import.

nodes.name: csvFxPricesData
nodes.summary: Reads and writes spot FX price series to CSV files, implementing the fxPricesData interface for the CSV backend.

nodes.name: data_blob.py
nodes.summary: Central dependency-injection container that lazily constructs and caches data-source objects (Mongo, Parquet, IB, CSV) and shared logging/config for the whole system.
nodes.languageNotes: The dataBlob dynamically resolves class names to storage backends via naming conventions, acting as a service locator.

nodes.name: dataBlob
nodes.summary: Service-locator object that wires together database connections, config and logging and lazily instantiates data classes on demand.

nodes.name: identifying_name
nodes.summary: Derives a canonical identifying name for a data class instance from its class name and backend, used for caching in the blob.

nodes.name: spotfx.py
nodes.summary: Abstract base for spot FX price data, providing currency-pair lookup, cross-rate derivation and update logic independent of storage backend.

nodes.name: fxPricesData
nodes.summary: Backend-agnostic spot FX price interface offering get/update of currency-pair price series and derivation of crosses against the default currency.

nodes.name: mongo_connection.py
nodes.summary: Manages MongoDB connectivity, providing a client factory, database wrapper and collection-connection helper plus host/int cleaning utilities.

nodes.name: mongoConnection
nodes.summary: Represents a connection to a specific Mongo collection, exposing the collection handle and connection metadata.

nodes.name: MongoClientFactory
nodes.summary: Singleton-style factory that creates and caches a single shared MongoClient per host configuration.

nodes.name: mongo_defaults
nodes.summary: Resolves Mongo host, database and port defaults from production config with fallbacks.

nodes.name: mongo_margin.py
nodes.summary: MongoDB-backed storage for margin time series, converting between the margin series objects and Mongo document entries.

nodes.name: mongoMarginData
nodes.summary: Stores and retrieves margin series in MongoDB, implementing the marginData interface for the Mongo backend.

nodes.name: test_mongodb.py
nodes.summary: Unit test verifying basic MongoDB connection behaviour against the mongo_connection module.

nodes.name: TestMongoDB
nodes.summary: Test case exercising MongoDB connection setup to confirm the connection wrapper works as expected.

nodes.name: margin.py
nodes.summary: Abstract margin data interface and the seriesOfMargin object representing a time series of account margin values.

nodes.name: marginData
nodes.summary: Backend-agnostic interface for reading and appending account margin series in the production system.

nodes.name: repocsv_spotfx_prices.py
nodes.summary: Initialisation script that copies repo spot FX price CSVs into the configured FX price store.

nodes.name: spotfx_from_csvAndInvestingDotCom_to_db.py
nodes.summary: Initialisation script importing spot FX prices from CSV and Investing.com files into the production FX database.

nodes.name: spotfx_from_csv_and_investing_dot_com
nodes.summary: Loads spot FX price series from CSV/Investing.com sources and writes them into the production currency data store.

nodes.name: spotfx_from_db_to_csv.py
nodes.summary: Initialisation script exporting spot FX prices from the production database back out to CSV files.

nodes.name: email_via_db_interface.py
nodes.summary: Production email layer that sends mail (with rate-limited warnings) and falls back to storing messages in the DB when email delivery fails.
nodes.languageNotes: Implements de-duplication of warning emails and store-and-forward of messages via a Mongo-backed control object.

nodes.name: dataEmailControl
nodes.summary: Mongo-backed control object tracking last-sent times for emails and stored-message handling to support rate limiting and retries.

nodes.name: send_email_and_record_date_or_store_on_fail
nodes.summary: Attempts to send a production email and, on failure, stores the message in the DB for later retry.

nodes.name: can_we_send_this_email_now
nodes.summary: Checks the recorded send history to decide whether a warning email may be sent now or should be throttled.

nodes.name: backtest_storage.py
nodes.summary: Provides the interactiveBacktest object that loads and navigates stored backtest System states for inspection in interactive sessions.

nodes.name: interactiveBacktest
nodes.summary: Wraps a pickled backtest System state, offering interactive menus to explore its stages, instruments and diagnostic outputs.

nodes.name: capital.py
nodes.summary: Capital accounting logic that updates total brokerage and system capital, handling P&L application and large-capital-change protection.

nodes.name: totalCapitalUpdater
nodes.summary: Computes updated broker, maximum and accumulated capital figures from new account values, guarding against implausibly large jumps.

nodes.name: roll_state.py
nodes.summary: Defines the futures roll-state enumeration and helper predicates governing which roll-state transitions and order generation are allowed.

nodes.name: allowable_roll_state_from_current_and_position
nodes.summary: Computes the set of valid next roll states given the current roll state and contract position.

nodes.name: clean_truncate_backtest_states.py
nodes.summary: Production housekeeping script that truncates old stored backtest state files to manage disk usage.

nodes.name: cleanTruncateBacktestStates
nodes.summary: Runnable cleanup object that deletes outdated backtest state files via the data blob.

nodes.name: clean_truncate_echo_files.py
nodes.summary: Production housekeeping script that truncates old echo (stdout capture) files to manage disk usage.

nodes.name: cleanTruncateEchoFiles
nodes.summary: Runnable cleanup object that removes outdated echo files from the production log directory.

nodes.name: clean_truncate_log_files.py
nodes.summary: Production housekeeping script that truncates old log records via the deprecated logs interface.

nodes.name: cleanTruncateLogFiles
nodes.summary: Runnable cleanup object that purges old log entries through the data blob.
